newsitem.title: USA: PanEnergy, Duke shareholders approve merger.
newsitem.headline: PanEnergy, Duke shareholders approve merger.

text.p: Duke Power Corp. and PanEnergy Corp. shareholders Thursday approved the $7.7 billion acquisition of Pannergy by Duke Power, the companies announced.

The merger of utility Duke Power and the natural gas company is awaiting final regulatory approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and remains on track to close in the third quarter, PanEnergy Chairman Paul Anderson said.
"We would expect a positive ruling due out some time in the next few months," Anderson told reporters after PanEnergy's shareholder meeting in Houston.

The proposed merger, approved earlier by state regulators, would form one of the largest U.S. energy and energy services companies ahead of expected deregulation of America's electric industry, the companies said.

Under the agreement, each PanEnergy common share would be converted into the right to receive 1.0444 shares of Duke Power common stock. The new company, to be called Duke Energy, will be based in Charlotte, N.C., Duke Power's current headquarters.

The merged company plans to be a national energy wholesaler and form alliances to sell into retail markets opened to competition, said Anderson, who will become Duke Energy's president and chief operating officer.
Duke Power stock fell 50 cents to $42.75 and PanEnergy dipped 75 cents to $42.75 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
